  4. The asset-monetization engine

Framework or proposal stage

An idle asset can become recurring income in five steps: audit, optimize, structure, operate and monetize.

HAYKALAH’s first programs on this engine are for government assets and are at framework or proposal stage. The private side, for family offices, developers and corporates, is rolling out.

Land, buildings and facilities that cost money to hold can be audited, re-planned, structured and operated to earn recurring income. HAYKALAH runs this as one engine, Audit → Optimize → Structure → Operate → Monetize, and can share in the revenue it creates. This explainer follows one asset through the five steps.

The shift

  • From an asset as a cost center, to an asset as a revenue platform.

  • From build, sell and exit, to own, optimize and earn through leases, concessions and revenue share.

  • From value at completion, to value based on utilization and cash flow.

Step by step

Step 1 of 5

Framework or proposal stage

Audit: find out what the asset costs and how it is used.

HAYKALAH builds an inventory, a utilization record and a cost baseline: what the asset costs to hold, how it is used and what holds it back. Whether a specific asset qualifies depends on this audit.

  • Asset owner to HAYKALAH Records and access to the asset
  • HAYKALAH to Asset owner Baseline: cost, use and what holds it back

All steps

  1. 01Audit: find out what the asset costs and how it is used.

    HAYKALAH builds an inventory, a utilization record and a cost baseline: what the asset costs to hold, how it is used and what holds it back. Whether a specific asset qualifies depends on this audit.

    • Asset owner to HAYKALAH Records and access to the asset
    • HAYKALAH to Asset owner Baseline: cost, use and what holds it back

  2. 02Optimize: choose what the asset should become.

    Highest-and-best-use analysis tests what the asset could become, followed by re-planning and activation. The new use, the contract and the vehicle are chosen as one decision.

    • HAYKALAH to The asset Highest-and-best-use analysis, re-planning and activation
    • HAYKALAH to Asset owner The use, the contract and the vehicle, as one decision

  3. 03Structure: put the asset in the right contract.

    The asset, or rights over it, is placed in a concession, a JV SPV, a Musataha, an Ijara or a revenue share, and in a fund or Sukuk at scale. The owner moves from building and selling to owning, optimizing and earning.

    • Asset owner to Structure The asset, or rights over it, under the chosen contract
    • Structure to Fund or Sukuk At scale: a fund or Sukuk, through licensed partners

  4. 04Operate: run it against KPIs.

    Operators are appointed under contract, and performance is measured from day one. The owner sees the results on one dashboard.

    • HAYKALAH to Operator Contract with KPIs
    • Operator to The asset Runs the asset
    • The asset to Asset owner Results on one dashboard

  5. 05Monetize: earn, refinance and recycle.

    Recurring income supports refinancing, and released capital moves to the next asset. HAYKALAH earns through fees, a share of the revenue the asset generates, or both, agreed asset by asset.

    • The asset to Asset owner Recurring income
    • Banks to Asset owner Refinancing once the asset earns
    • Asset owner to Next asset Released capital
    • Asset owner to HAYKALAH Fees, a share of the revenue, or both

Who it suits

  • Sovereign and government entities with estates, venues and facilities.

  • Family offices and trusts with idle land, under-let malls and hotels, or staff housing.

  • Founders and private investors who own income assets or corporate estates.

  • Banks and financial institutions that refinance assets once they earn.

Risks and conditions

  • The audit decides. Typical candidates are idle land, under-let malls and hotels, staff housing, corporate estates, stadiums and cultural venues, but whether a specific asset qualifies depends on the audit.

  • The programs are early. HAYKALAH’s government programs are at framework or proposal stage, and proposals and frameworks are not mandates.

  • The contract has to be precise. A revenue share must define revenue exactly, say how it is measured and reported, and set when payments are made.

  • The operator carries the day-to-day. The income depends on how the asset is run, which is why the operator works under contract and against KPIs.

  • Refinancing needs records. Capital recycling depends on records that lenders and investors trust: a history of income, an up-to-date model and complete documents.

  • Regulated steps and approvals. A fund or Sukuk is a regulated activity, executed through appropriately licensed partners, and any fund is set up and managed by a CMA-authorised manager. Shariah structures are subject to Shariah board approval.

  • No guarantee of approvals, financing or returns.
